title: Is it inefficient for an entire game to be coded onto an HTML?
author: Pandaman_323
selftext:
I'm making a personal game and admittedly am not a coder whatsoever, so don't worry about me trying to advertise or sell the game to you lmao.

I've been messing around with vibecoding numerous board games the past couple weeks. I've noticed that my first game was only built in a single HTML file, and generally takes up a lot of tokens to even make the simplest of bugfixes. Meanwhile, from game #2 onward, Claude is coding the games almost exclusively in .js files and HTML is used simply to just launch the game, and bug fixing seems to use much less tokens.  
  
My question is, is that I assume the JavaScript coding methods used on game #2 make it easier for Claude to locate and tweak parts of the game, thus lower token usage? If this is the case, is it possible/worthwhile to ask Claude to convert game #1's coding structure to game #2's?

comments.author: Minimum_Lock_1906
comments.body: Pelo que você descreveu, é provável que o motivo seja o primeiro jogo ter sido escrito em um único arquivo. Dessa forma, sempre que é necessário fazer uma alteração a IA lê o jogo inteiramente para executar a tarefa. No segundo jogo, como os arquivos devem estar divididos por classes, a IA lê apenas aqueles que fazem sentido para a execução da tarefa, permitindo que ela não leia partes irrelevantes do código para tal.

replies.author: Pandaman_323
replies.body: Makes sense. So would it be worthwhile to ask Claude to re-write the first game to emulate game 2's file structure? I assume it would be costly in terms of tokens?

replies.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
replies.body: Tell it to create a rule that if a single file is larger than about 15kb, it needs to be split without violating ownership boundaries.

replies.author: pickleunicorn
replies.body: 15kb is waaaaay too big for a file with source code

replies.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
replies.body:
It really depends on what it is. Normally I'd agree, but sometimes there is legitimately no way to seperate it without making boundaries worse.  For example, everything in ability.go needs to be there.  Separating it would both make readability worse and cause confusion on where ownership lies.  The answer to making that easier to digest for AI is to have pointer maps with symbol lookup tables, so it never needs to load the entire file.  There are hundreds of .go files for my server, but I can finish a session at <300k context most of the time.

https://preview.redd.it/i4duz4u1i5vh1.png?width=1910&format=png&auto=webp&s=1e5b9ee740ed07b1faf5d894af34157634a8a143

replies.author: pickleunicorn
replies.body: It's just a question of good architecture and factorisation IMO. And Claude is not good at that ahah

replies.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
replies.body: Not by default, for sure.  Having 20+ years of experience before AI came around helps haha.

replies.author: Pandaman_323
replies.body: And in my case, have 0 years of experience hurts lmao

replies.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
replies.body: Look into "Domain Driven Design" even if you don't understand it, claude does, and it can help you structure your project for it.  It will help immensely as your project gets larger

replies.author: Pandaman_323
replies.body: Reading up on it now, thank you for the lead

replies.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
replies.body: Don't take it as a "I must fully follow it" either. Software patterns are best used in the ways that actually fit what you're doing. For example DDD is good for making ownership boundaries, but for a game you wouldn't want all the abstractions that come with it.. so you might have a mix of DDD and Entity Component System, or even a slimmed version of it.

replies.author: pickleunicorn
replies.body: Yeah, doesn't help at all. I think you should at list ask to Claude to tell you some basics of each language used in your games to understand at least the system. It will help you to give him directions. Because the overall issue is to create clunky code that will be hard to maintain for Claude, unoptimized and buggy. You should try to search for skills to add. You even could ask him to create a skill to maintain a good architecture for Godot, or the best way to keep a good factorisation and good responsibility concerns in the source code, and best practices for the type of language it's using, etc

replies.author: Pandaman_323
replies.body: Makes sense - yeah I'm figuring it out as I go, I imagine in a year I'll look back on these projects and scoff at em lmao.

replies.author: pickleunicorn
replies.body: Ahah, the same. Btw I'm a bit concerned with the junior devs nowadays because they will never have the chance to learn that...

replies.author: Minimum_Lock_1906
replies.body: Sim, é você vai refazer o jogo praticamente do 0. O conceito que estamos conversando aqui se chama desenvolvimento orientado a objetos (recomendo perguntar a própria IA sobre ele, minimamente). HTML não permite que você desenvolva seguindo esse conceito, então terá que ser refeito em Javascript, mas é extremamente recomendado visto que HTML não é uma linguagem criada para o backend.

replies.author: pickleunicorn
replies.body: It's certain that the game is already in js, wrapped up in the html file. Also, the game as nothing to do with backend code.

comments.author: Similar_Guide4193
comments.body:
Splitting up work into different files is good practice because you are seperating concerns as much as possible.

Also, You can tell AI to compile all of these files into a single HTML file whenever it's done whenever it finishes working on the source. We would call this making a build.

You can even take this a step further. For example, you can tell AI to encode pngs,any other asset file etc as base64 and include the base64 text in the HTML itself for it to be decoded into the png/asset again at runtime.

replies.author: Pandaman_323
replies.body: Gotcha that makes sense. So should I ask Claude to unwrap the HTML to have it separate the files back to the 'development' build?

replies.author: Similar_Guide4193
replies.body:
I'm guessing you have a bunch of files now? When you make a build you wrap a copy of all your source files into the build. You don't unwrap back and you're free to delete the build when you don't need it anymore.

\[edit\] And yes you can ask AI to just build the game as a single HTML file and it should understand what you want. Just ensure the source files have a backup/git etc they shouldn't be touched during the build process.

replies.author: Pandaman_323
replies.body:
I think you're misunderstanding my last comment.

Game #1 was only coded within an HTML build - the HTML is 9mb large lol. The JavaScript files never existed on my hard drive. Thus, whenever I ask for a bugfix, it takes like 10% Claude usage minimum. Should I ask Clade to unwrap the HTML so it unpacks the JavaScript files so I don't need to burn so much usage just to make the tiniest change to the code?

replies.author: Similar_Guide4193
replies.body: Ahh, ok I misunderstood. You are right, make a backup of your single HTML file. and tell it to unwrap  the single HTML file.

replies.author: Pandaman_323
replies.body: Perfect, I'll give it a go tomorrow. Thank you!

comments.author: count023
comments.body:
Use the right tools for the right job. Js is good for logic, file handling and such. Html and CSS are for presentation and playback. 

It's not a case of using one thing for all, it's a case of using the right thing at the right time

replies.author: Pandaman_323
replies.body: Yeah that's starting to click for me right now. So I should ask Claude to decompile/unwrap game #1's HTML?

replies.author: count023
replies.body: the correct term is "refactor". You tell Claude to review the game in HTML and "refactor it" to "move logic and handling elements into Javascript where appropriate". Claude will be pretty good at telling you which bits it thinks shoud go and which should say. Tell it your focus is to seperate out data handling, logic and presentation elements.

replies.author: Pandaman_323
replies.body: Okay great - yeah that's what I was thinking I just didn't know the terminology. I'll give this a go tomorrow
